name: Clarification reply arrives → stamp agent.run.clarification_resumed
description:
ADR-053 Phase 4b-2 PR-2 — the interactive-RESUME marker (half 1 of the 2-step marker, the mirror of pause rules 07/08). When a coordinator loop re-enters as a clarification REPLY (the operator answered the question rule 07/08 paused on), this stamps agent.run.clarification_resumed on the RUN entity via the subject override $entity.triple.agent.run.entity_id; rule 11 consumes the marker, transitions awaiting_approval→executing, and clears both clarification markers.

WHY a single rule (no 07/08-style anchor split): on resume the reply re-enters carrying the run anchor DIRECTLY — semstreams#256 (U1) threads the run's RunID onto the reply TaskMessage, so graph_writer stamps agent.run.entity_id on the reply loop regardless of which anchor branch the original ask used. So unlike the pause markers (which split because some recovery coordinators carry only lineage), the resume marker keys on agent.run.entity_id alone.

THE REPLY DISCRIMINATOR (lineage.clarification-reply ne ""): a loop-local signal that distinguishes a clarification reply from any other coordinator loop in the run (every run coordinator carries agent.run.entity_id, so the anchor alone is NOT enough). Per semstreams#256 Thread 2 (preferred shape), the SemTeams reply client sets metadata[agent.related_loops]={"clarification-reply":"<asking loop / run>"} on the reply; graph_writer's WriteLineageTriples turns it into a queryable lineage.clarification-reply triple on the reply loop. THE TYPED ALTERNATIVE (semstreams#256 Thread 2 alt) is a first-class agent.loop.reply_to predicate — if upstream picks that, this condition's field becomes agent.loop.reply_to (a one-line swap). NOTE: lineage.* is being used here for a non-lineage pointer (the 3rd such consumer; see [[lineage-passthrough-pattern]]); a dedicated properties.*/reply.* namespace upstream would be cleaner and is called out in #256.

INERT UNTIL #256: today the reply path drops BOTH the run anchor and msg.Metadata (component.go:716-723), so a real reply loop carries NEITHER agent.run.entity_id NOR lineage.clarification-reply → this rule cannot fire in production. The behavioral mock journey (clarification-resume) is DEFERRED to #256's landing — when the reply path threads the trigger fields, the journey will drive the resume FOR REAL (no seeding; the e2e harness has no triple-write seam, and a seeded fake would assert the seed shape rather than the real wire). Until then the slice is pinned STRUCTURALLY by the agent_run_pack contract tests (resume marker + ordered marker-clear + the rule-09 bounce guard). This is the buildable-now half of PR-2.

metadata.joins_with: 11-resume-awaiting-to-executing.json (consumes the marker + transitions + clears) and 07/08 (the pause markers this resumes).
metadata.marker_object: $entity.instance records WHICH loop carried the reply (mirrors 07/08's clarification_pending=$entity.instance).
metadata.single_rule_no_split: Keys on agent.run.entity_id alone — semstreams#256 (U1) threads the run anchor onto the reply, so the reply loop always carries agent.run.entity_id regardless of the original ask's anchor branch. Unlike the pause-marker pair 07/08.
metadata.reply_discriminator: lineage.clarification-reply — the preferred semstreams#256 Thread-2 shape (related_loops→lineage.* channel, no new vocab). Typed alternative agent.loop.reply_to is a one-line field swap. lineage.* reuse for a non-lineage pointer is the 3rd consumer (see [[lineage-passthrough-pattern]]); #256 calls out a properties.* namespace.
metadata.inert_until: semstreams#256 — the reply path currently drops both the run anchor and msg.Metadata, so a real reply loop carries neither trigger field. Pinned structurally by the agent_run_pack contract tests now; the behavioral clarification-resume journey is deferred to #256's landing (will drive the real reply path, no seeding).
metadata.autonomous_inertness: 4b-2 is interactive-only by construction (the pause it resumes never happens in autonomous mode — decide(ask_user) is rejected pre-stamp under restricted_decide_actions). No separate gate needed.
